name: Pearl Beige
lede: Pearl Beige is a muted taupe-brown standardized as RAL 1035, and one of the most common colors in our entire painting archive.

sections.title: A RAL standard, not a pearl
sections.body:
ColorHub's library sets this swatch to RAL 1035, part of the RAL system used across European paint, design and industry since the 1920s [1]. Despite the name, nothing in the library ties it to an actual pearl; *pearl* here works as a soft-sheen qualifier, the way it does across several beiges and greys in the same system [1]. RAL names like this one describe a specific, repeatable paint batch rather than a natural or historical object, which is why the library gives it no first-recorded date the way it can for Ridgway or Maerz and Paul names [1]. The nearest everyday name on file is [[taupe]], about 3.2 units of ΔE away [1].

[[tan]], [[ecru]] and [[silver]] sit nearby in the same warm-neutral family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Pearl Beige in 3,991 of 23,781 paintings (16.78 percent), as photographed, making it one of the more common colors on file, roughly steady across every century from the 1100s to the 1900s [2]. It runs highest in Chinese and Japanese painting, over twice the archive rate, led by Shen Zhou, Kano Tan'yū and the Dutch painter Jan van Goyen [2]. It keeps company with Taupe, Silver and Ecru more than chance [2]. These are screen approximations of aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
